jobs.tierReason: review of owner-configured command hooks run by the merge queue (smoke and preview deploy), environment handling, and approval-hash changes
jobs.prompt: Review coordination/review/ci.diff with the new module tools/ci-hooks.mjs and the design in docs/plans/phase15-lessons-design.md section 10. Rules that must hold: (1) a hook only runs commands from the project's own profile in .project-swarm.json, never from a worker output, ticket, manifest, lesson or run state; a worker cannot change the profile ci block through a batch (check the existing profile-change guard covers the new key, since a batch that edits the ci argv would run attacker commands on the owner's machine with the owner's rights) ; (2) no shell is used and argv cannot be altered by file names or ticket text; (3) secrets: secret-looking environment variables are not passed, and nothing from the hook output (tail, summary, fix ticket notes, journal events, warnings) can contain a secret, an email or a home path, including the text sent to the local brain or the Haiku fallback for the summary (sensitive projects); (4) the preview production refusal cannot be bypassed (case, quoting, joined flags like --prod=true, target=production, a script that wraps the command) or, if it cannot be made complete, the docs say plainly that it is a safety net and not a guarantee; (5) a failing or hanging hook (timeout, process group kill, huge output, a hook that spawns background processes) cannot hang the queue, leak processes, corrupt the run state or roll back a batch; (6) origin ci tickets: they are excluded from the approval hash, so check this cannot be abused to run unapproved work (who can write origin ci into the ledger, does validateTicket or readLedger let a worker-written ticket carry origin ci, can a ticket claim origin ci to skip approval, scope refs, acceptance or sensitivity rules, and is the Failure summary line in prompts safe as flat capped text); (7) skeleton gating cannot be used to starve or bypass the approval, and --skip-skeleton only affects one run. Find real bugs with file and line evidence, rank high, medium, low, and say how to fix each. Do not edit files.
